def test_sort_array():
    # Empty input returns empty list
    assert sort_array([]) == []

    # Single element (first+last even -> descending, but trivially same)
    assert sort_array([5]) == [5]
    assert sort_array([0]) == [0]

    # first + last odd -> ascending sort
    assert sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5]) == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]   # 2+5=7 odd
    assert sort_array([1, 2, 3, 4]) == [1, 2, 3, 4]               # 1+4=5 odd
    assert sort_array([3, 1, 2]) == [1, 2, 3]                     # 3+2=5 odd

    # first + last even -> descending sort
    assert sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5, 6]) == [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]  # 2+6=8 even
    assert sort_array([1, 2, 3, 5]) == [5, 3, 2, 1]                    # 1+5=6 even
    assert sort_array([5, 1, 3]) == [5, 3, 1]                          # 5+3=8 even

    # Duplicates
    assert sort_array([1, 1, 1]) == [1, 1, 1]

    # Negative numbers (Python modulo: -7 % 2 == 1 -> odd; -6 % 2 == 0 -> even)
    assert sort_array([-4, -2, -3]) == [-4, -3, -2]  # sum -7 odd -> ascending
    assert sort_array([-2, -3, -4]) == [-2, -3, -4]  # sum -6 even -> descending
